name: SSH Keys
description: Generate Ed25519, ECDSA and RSA key pairs, inspect fingerprints and randomart, and change passphrases
help: Generate: choose Ed25519 (recommended), ECDSA or RSA, add a comment and an optional passphrase. Keys are created in the OpenSSH format used by ssh-keygen and can be saved with the right permissions (private key readable only by you).

Inspect: paste or open a public key, a private key, an authorized_keys file or a known_hosts file to see each key's type, size, comment, SHA256 and MD5 fingerprints and randomart — the same values ssh-keygen -lv shows.
Encrypted private keys show their fingerprint without the passphrase; enter it to check that it is correct.
Old PEM RSA private keys (BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY or BEGIN PRIVATE KEY) are converted to the OpenSSH format.
Passphrase: add, change or remove the passphrase of an OpenSSH private key.
Keys are generated with the operating system's secure random number generator and never leave this computer.

generate.title: New key

hint.ed25519: Recommended: short, fast and secure. Supported by OpenSSH 6.5+ and GitHub, GitLab and most servers.
hint.ecdsa: NIST curves, for systems that require them.
hint.rsa: For old systems that do not support Ed25519. Use at least 3072 bits.

generate.emptyHint: The public key goes into authorized_keys or your Git hosting settings; keep the private key secret
generate.privateHint: Never share the private key. Anyone who has it can sign in as you.
